title: Housing protesters clash with police in Lisbon and Porto over rental bill
seoTitle: Lisbon housing protest clashes with police

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against soaring housing costs and a government rental bill.
tea.want: Participants demanded that the government scrap plans to make evictions easier and end rent caps.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Activist group Acampada Lisboa called for a fresh rally following police clearing operations.

summary: Housing protesters in Lisbon and Porto clashed with police after authorities moved in to clear protest camps set up in city squares. Thousands had initially participated in marches protesting against a contentious rental bill and high living costs in Portugal. Police equipped with shields and batons dismantled tents at Rossio Square in Lisbon and Dom Joao I Square in Porto, citing refusals to disperse. According to police statements, multiple officers and demonstrators sustained injuries during the operations, and over a dozen individuals were arrested across both cities. Activist groups criticized the police response as excessive and organized follow-up rallies to contest the evictions. Meanwhile, the government maintained its legislative stance while acknowledging potential modifications.
demands: Scrap plans to make evictions easier
End rent caps on new leases
response: Police used shields and batons to dismantle protest camps and disperse demonstrators, resulting in 13 arrests and multiple injuries among officers and civilians. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro ruled out withdrawing the bill.

arrests.text: Six people were arrested in Lisbon and seven in Porto

updates.text: Police moved in to clear protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, leading to clashes and arrests.
Demonstrators began to demobilize in Lisbon and Porto following the police operations.
